resources.string: Tap the button below when you park and ParkSpot remembers exactly where you left the car.
Alerts before your parking time runs out
This device has no compass, so only the distance is shown.
Compass accuracy is low — wave the phone in a figure of eight to calibrate it.
ParkSpot needs your location to save and find your parking spot. Nothing ever leaves your phone.
Could not get a location fix. Move somewhere with a clearer view of the sky and try again.
Save the spot on its own when your car\'s Bluetooth disconnects — which is the moment you step out of the car.
Save the spot when the car disconnects
No paired Bluetooth devices. Pair your car stereo in system settings first.
Turn Bluetooth on to see your paired devices.
ParkSpot needs Bluetooth access to notice your car connecting and disconnecting.
Reconnecting to the car also clears the saved spot, since you are driving again.
Saving your spot when the car disconnects
Could not get a GPS fix when you parked. Open ParkSpot to save the spot by hand.
Android blocked ParkSpot from saving your spot. Set Location to \"Allow all the time\" in Settings and it will work with the app closed.
Set to \"Allow all the time\", so the spot can be saved with the app closed.
Automatic parking needs Location set to \"Allow all the time\". Without it Android has to be asked for a foreground service instead, and on this phone it refused.
Android would not let ParkSpot save your spot in the background. Open the app to save it by hand.
ParkSpot needs location access to save your spot automatically.
ParkSpot can wake up when your car disconnects, even when it is closed. Nothing runs in between, so it costs no battery.
Battery optimisation is on for ParkSpot, so Android may stop it waking up when your car disconnects. Set it to \"Unrestricted\" to make automatic parking reliable.
This device has no battery-optimisation screen.
Past parking spots show up here.
Delete every past parking spot and its photos? The car you are parked at now is kept.
